title: Egyptian fractions
summary: Writing rationals as sums of distinct $1/n$. Every rational has such representations; the questions are how short, how small the denominators, and which colourings or dense sets must contain a representation of $1$.
key_statements: \text{any } r\text{-colouring of } \mathbb N \text{ has a monochromatic } \textstyle\sum 1/n_i = 1 \ \text{(Croot 2003)}

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #316
research_problems.statement:
Is it true that if $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}\setminus\{1\}$ is a finite set with
$\sum_{n \in A} \frac{1}{n} < 2$ then there is a partition $A=A_1 \sqcup A_2$
such that $\sum_{n \in A_i} \frac{1}{n} < 1$ for $i=1,2$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #46
research_problems.statement:
Does every finite colouring of the integers have a monochromatic solution to
$1=\sum \frac{1}{n_i}$ with $2\leq n_1<\cdots <n_k$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #296
research_problems.statement: Let $N\geq 1$ and let $k(N)$ be maximal such that there are $k$ disjoint $A_1,\ldots,A_k\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ with $\sum_{n\in A_i}\frac{1}{n}=1$ for all $i$. Estimate $k(N)$. Is it true that $k(N)=o(\log N)$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #290
research_problems.statement:
Let $a\geq 1$. Must there exist some $b>a$ such that
$$\sum_{a\leq n\leq b}\frac{1}{n}=\frac{r_1}{s_1}\textrm{ and }
\sum_{a\leq n\leq b+1}\frac{1}{n}=\frac{r_2}{s_2},$$
with $(r_i,s_i)=1$ and $s_2<s_1$? If so, how does this $b(a)$ grow with $a$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #242
research_problems.statement:
For every $n>2$ there exist distinct integers $1 ≤ x < y < z$
such that $\frac 4 n = \frac 1 x + \frac 1 y + \frac 1 z$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #310
research_problems.statement:
Let $\alpha >0$ and $N\geq 1$. Is it true that for any $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ with
$\lvert A\rvert \geq \alpha N$ there exists some $S\subseteq A$ such that
$$\frac{a}{b}=\sum_{n\in S}\frac{1}{n}$$
with $a\leq b =O_\alpha(1)$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #206
research_problems.statement:
Let $x>0$ be a real number. For any $n\geq 1$ let
$$R_n(x) = \sum_{i=1}^n\frac{1}{m_i}<x$$
be the maximal sum of $n$ distinct unit fractions which is $<x$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #299
research_problems.statement:
Is there an infinite sequence $a_1 < a_2 < \dots$ such that $a_{i+1} - a_i = O(1)$ and no finite
sum of $\frac{1}{a_i}$ is equal to 1?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #148
research_problems.statement:
Let $F(k)$ be the number of solutions to
$$ 1= \frac{1}{n_1}+\cdots+\frac{1}{n_k},$$
where $1\leq n_1<\cdots<n_k$ are distinct integers. Find good estimates for $F(k)$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #300
research_problems.statement:
Let $A(N)$ denote the maximal cardinality of $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ such that
$\sum_{n\in S}\frac{1}{n}\neq 1$ for all $S\subseteq A$. Estimate $A(N)$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #306
research_problems.statement:
Let $\frac a b\in \mathbb{Q}_{>0}$ with $b$ squarefree. Are there integers $1 < n_1 < \dots < n_k$,
each the product of two distinct primes, such that $\frac{a}{b}=\frac{1}{n_1}+\cdots+\frac{1}{n_k}$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #287
research_problems.statement:
Let $k\geq2$. Is it true that, for any distinct integers
$1 < n_1 < \cdots < n_k$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^k \frac{1}{n_i} = 1$,
we must have $\max(n_{i+1} - n_i) \geq 3$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #295
research_problems.statement:
Let $k(N)$ denote the smallest $k$ such that there exists
$N ≤ n_1 < ⋯ < n_k$ with $\frac 1 {n_1} + ... + \frac 1 {n_k} = 1$

Is it true that $\lim_{N \to \infty} k(N) - (e - 1)N = \infty$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #313
research_problems.statement:
Are there infinitely many pairs `(m, P)` where `m ≥ 2` is an integer
and `P` is a set of distinct primes such that the following equation holds:
$\sum_{p \in P} \frac{1}{p} = 1 - \frac{1}{m}$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #294
research_problems.statement:
Let $N\geq 1$ and let $t(N)$ be the least integer $t$ such that there is no solution to
$$1=\frac{1}{n_1}+\cdots+\frac{1}{n_k}$$
with $t=n_1<\cdots <n_k\leq N$. Estimate $t(N)$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #292
research_problems.statement:
Let $A$ be the set of $n\in \mathbb{N}$ such that there exist $1\leq m_1<\cdots <m_k=n$ with
$\sum\tfrac{1}{m_i}=1$. Explore $A$. In particular, does $A$ have density $1$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #291
research_problems.statement:
(a) Let $n\geq 1$ and define $L_n$ to be the least common multiple of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and $a_n$ by
$\sum_{1\leq k\leq n}\frac{1}{k}=\frac{a_n}{L_n}$.

Is it true that $(a_n,L_n)=1$ occurs for infinitely many $n$?

(b) Is it true that $(a_n,L_n)>1$ occurs for infinitely many $n$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #288
research_problems.statement:
Is it true that there are only finitely many pairs of intervals $I_1$, $I_2$ such that
$$
\sum_{n_1 \in I_1} \frac{1}{n_1} + \sum_{n_2 \in I_2} \frac{1}{n_2} \in \mathbb{N}?
$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #315
research_problems.statement:
Let $u_1=1$ and $u_{n+1}=u_n(u_n+1)$, so that $\sum_{k\geq 1}\frac{1}{u_k+1}$ and
$u_k=\lfloor c_0^{2^k}+1\rfloor$ for $k\geq 1$, where
$$c_0=\lim u_n^{1/2^n}=1.264085\cdots.$$
Let $a_1<a_2<\cdots $ be any other sequence with $\sum \frac{1}{a_k}=1$. Is it true that
$$\liminf a_n^{1/2^n}<c_0=1.264085\cdots?$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #307
research_problems.statement:
Are there two finite set of primes $P$ and $Q$ such that

$$
1 = \left( \sum_{p \in P} \frac{1}{p} \right) \left( \sum_{q \in Q} \frac{1}{q} \right)
$$
?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #318
research_problems.statement:
(a) There exists a set `A` with positive density that does not have property `P₁`.
#TODO: prove this lemma by assuming `erdos_318.contain_single_even`.

(b) Does the set of squares excluding 1 have property `P₁`?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #305
research_problems.statement:
For integers $1\leq a<b$ let $D(a,b)$ be the minimal value of $n_k$ such that there exist
integers $1\leq n_1<\cdots <n_k$ with
$$\frac{a}{b}=\frac{1}{n_1}+\cdots+\frac{1}{n_k}.$$
Estimate $D(b)=\max_{1\leq a<b}D(a,b)$. Is it true that
$$D(b) \ll b(\log b)^{1+o(1)}?$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #45
research_problems.statement:
Let $k\geq 2$. Is there an integer $n_k$ such that, if $D=\{ 1<d<n_k : d\mid n_k\}$, then for any
$k$-colouring of $D$ there is a monochromatic subset $D'\subseteq D$ such that
$\sum_{d\in D'}\frac{1}{d}=1$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #282
research_problems.statement:
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be an infinite set and consider the following
greedy algorithm for a rational $x\in (0,1)$: choose the minimal $n\in A$ not used
so far such that $n\geq 1/x$ and repeat with $x$ replaced by $x-\frac{1}{n}$. If this
terminates after finitely many steps then this produces a representation of
$x$ as the sum of distinct unit fractions with denominators from $A$.

Does this process always terminate if $x$ has odd denominator and $A$ is the
set of odd numbers?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #312
research_problems.statement:
Does there exist a constant `c > 0` such that, for any `K > 1`, whenever `A` is a sufficiently large
finite multiset of integers with $\sum_{n \in A} 1/n > K$ there exists some $S \subseteq A$ such that
$1 - \exp(-(c*K)) < \sum_{n \in S} 1/n \le 1$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #286
research_problems.statement:
Let $k\geq 2$. Is it true that there exists an interval $I$ of width $(e-1+o(1))k$ and integers
$n_1<\cdots<n_k\in I$ such that
$$1=\frac{1}{n_1}+\cdots+\frac{1}{n_k}?$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #285
research_problems.statement:
Let $f(k)$ be the minimal value of $n_k$ such that there exist $n_1 < n_2 < \dots < n_k$ with
$$
  1 = \frac{1}{n_1} + \cdots + \frac{1}{n_k}.
$$
Is it true that
$$
  f(k) = (1 + o(1)) \frac{e}{e - 1} k ?
$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #303
research_problems.statement:
Is it true that in any finite colouring of the integers there exists a monochromatic solution
to $\frac 1 a = \frac 1 b + \frac 1 c$ with distinct $a, b, c$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #289
research_problems.statement:
Is it true that, for all sufficiently large $k$, there exist finite intervals
$I_1, \dotsc, I_k \subset \mathbb{N}$, distinct, not overlapping or adjacent, with
$|I_i| \geq 2$ for $1 \leq i \leq k$ such that
$$
1 = \sum_{i=1}^k \sum_{n \in I_i} \frac{1}{n}?
$$
Here two intervals are adjacent if their union is again an interval, so any two of the
$I_i$ must be separated by at least one integer.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #321
research_problems.statement:
Let $R(N)$ be the size of the largest $A\subseteq\{1, ..., N\}$ such that all sums
$\sum_{n\in S} \frac{1}{n}$ are distinct for $S\subseteq A$.

Let $R(N)$ be the size of the largest $A\subseteq\{1, ..., N\}$ such that all sums
$\sum_{n\in S} \frac{1}{n}$ are distinct for $S\subseteq A$. What is $R(N)$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #283
research_problems.statement:
Let $p\colon \mathbb{Z} \rightarrow \mathbb{Z}$ be a polynomial (with rational coefficients,
taking integer values at all integers) whose leading coefficient is positive and such that there
exists no $d≥2$ with $d ∣ p(n)$ for all $n≥1$. Is it true that,
for all sufficiently large $m$, there exist integers $1≤n_1<\dots < n_k$ such that
$$1=\frac{1}{n_1}+\cdots+\frac{1}{n_k}$$
and
$$m=p(n_1)+\cdots+p(n_k)$$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #311
research_problems.statement:
Let $\delta(N)$ be the minimal non-zero value of $\lvert 1-\sum_{n\in A}\frac{1}{n}\rvert$ as $A$
ranges over all subsets of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$. Is it true that
$$\delta(N)=e^{-(c+o(1))N}$$
for some constant $c\in (0,1)$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #314
research_problems.statement:
Let $n\geq 1$ and let $m$ be minimal such that $\sum_{n\leq k\leq m}\frac{1}{k}\geq 1$. We define
$$\epsilon(n) = \sum_{n\leq k\leq m}\frac{1}{k}-1.$$
How small can $\epsilon(n)$ be? Is it true that
$$\liminf n^2\epsilon(n)=0?$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #319
research_problems.statement:
What is the size of the largest $A\subseteq\{1, \dots, N\}$ such that there is a function
$\delta : A \to \{-1, 1\}$ such that
$$
  \sum_{n\in A} \frac{\delta n}{n} = 0
$$
and
$$
  \sum_{n\in A'}\frac{\delta n}{n} \neq 0
$$
for all non-empty $A'\subsetneq A$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #309
research_problems.statement:
Let $N\geq 1$. How many integers can be written as the sum of distinct unit fractions with
denominators from $\{1,\ldots,N\}$? Are there $o(\log N)$ such integers?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #825
research_problems.statement:
Is there an absolute constant $C > 0$ such that every integer $n$ with
$\sigma(n) > Cn$ is the distinct sum of proper divisors of $n$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #355
research_problems.statement:
Is there a lacunary sequence $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ (so that $A=\{a_1 < \cdots\}$ and
there exists some $\lambda > 1$ such that $a_{n+1}/a_n\geq \lambda$ for all $n\geq 1$) such that
$$\left\{ \sum_{a\in A'}\frac{1}{a} : A'\subseteq A\textrm{ finite}\right\}$$
contain all rationals in some open interval?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #47
research_problems.statement: If $\delta>0$ and $N$ is sufficiently large in terms of $\delta$, and $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ is such that $\sum_{a\in A}\frac{1}{a}>\delta \log N$ then must there exist $S\subseteq A$ such that $\sum_{n\in S}\frac{1}{n}=1$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #302
research_problems.statement:
(a) Let $f(N)$ be the size of the largest $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ such that there are no
solutions to
$$\frac{1}{a}= \frac{1}{b}+\frac{1}{c}$$
with distinct $a,b,c\in A$? Estimate $f(N)$.

(b) In particular, is $f(N)=(\tfrac{1}{2}+o(1))N$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #317
research_problems.statement:
Is there some constant $c>0$ such that for every $n\geq 1$ there exists some $\delta_k\in \{-1,0,1\}$ for $1\leq k\leq n$ with
$$0< \left\lvert \sum_{1\leq k\leq n}\frac{\delta_k}{k}\right\rvert < \frac{c}{2^n}?$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #298
research_problems.statement:
Does every set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ of positive density contain some finite $S \subset A$ such that
$\sum_{n \in S} \frac{1}{n} = 1$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #308
research_problems.statement:
(a) Let $N\geq 1$. What is the smallest integer not representable as the sum of distinct unit
fractions with denominators from $\{1,\ldots,N\}$?

(b) Let $N\geq 1$. Is it true that the set of integers representable as the sum of distinct unit
fractions with denominators from $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ has the shape $\{1,\ldots,m\}$ for some $m$?

title: Covering systems
summary: A finite set of congruences $a_i \bmod n_i$ covering every integer, such as $0\bmod2,\ 0\bmod3,\ 1\bmod4,\ 5\bmod6,\ 7\bmod12$. Hough (2015) proved the smallest modulus of a covering with distinct moduli is bounded.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #7
research_problems.statement: Is there a covering system all of whose moduli are odd (and greater than 1)?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #273
research_problems.statement: Is there a covering system all of whose moduli are of the form $p-1$ for some primes $p \geq 5$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #280
research_problems.statement:
Let $n_1<n_2<\cdots $ be an infinite sequence of integers with associated $a_k\pmod{n_k}$, such that for some $\epsilon>0$ we have $n_k>(1+\epsilon)k\log k$ for all $k$. Then
$$
\#\{ m<n_k : m\not\equiv a_i\pmod{n_i} \textrm{ for }1\leq i\leq k\}\neq o(k).
$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1188
research_problems.statement:
Call a set of distinct integers $1<n_1<\cdots<n_k$ with associated congruence
classes $a_i\pmod{n_i}$ a distinct covering system if every integer satisfies at
least one of these congruences. A minimal distinct covering system is one such
that no proper subset forms a covering system. Let $F(x)$ count the number of
minimal distinct covering systems with all moduli in $[1,x]$. Estimate $F(x)$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #947
research_problems.statement:
There is no exact covering system - that is, a finite collection of congruence classes
$a_i\pmod{n_i}$ with distinct $n_i$ such that every integer satisfies exactly one of these
congruence classes.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #274
research_problems.statement:
If $G$ is a group, can there exist an exact covering of $G$ by more than one coset
of different sizes? (i.e. each element is contained in exactly one of the cosets.)

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #275
research_problems.statement:
If a finite system of $r$ congruences $\{ a_i\pmod{n_i} : 1\leq i\leq r\}$ (the $n_i$ are not
necessarily distinct) covers $2^r$ consecutive integers then it covers all integers.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #2
research_problems.statement: Can the smallest modulus of a covering system be arbitrarily large?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #203
research_problems.statement:
Is there an integer $m$ with $(m, 6) = 1$ such that none of $2^k \cdot 3^\ell \cdot m + 1$ are prime,
for any $k, \ell \ge 0$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #586
research_problems.statement: Is there a covering system such that no two of the moduli divide each other?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #204
research_problems.statement:
Are there $n$ such that there is a covering system with moduli the divisors of $n$ which is 'as
disjoint as possible'?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1113
research_problems.statement:
Do there exist Sierpiński numbers that possess no finite covering set
of primes?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #277
research_problems.statement:
Is it true that, for every $c$, there exists an $n$ such that $\sigma(n)>cn$ but there is no
covering system whose moduli all divide $n$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #276
research_problems.statement:
Is there an infinite Lucas sequence $a_0, a_1, \ldots$ where $a_{n+2} = a_{n+1} + a_n$ for
$n \ge 0$ such that all $a_k$ are composite, and yet no integer has a common factor with every
term of the sequence?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1190
research_problems.statement:
Let
$$\epsilon_m=\max \sum \frac{1}{n_i}$$
where the maximum is taken over all finite sequences $m<n_1<\cdots<n_k$ for which there exist
congruences $a_i\pmod{n_i}$ such that no integer satisfies two such congruences.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #202
research_problems.statement:
Let $n_1<\cdots < n_r\leq N$ with associated $a_i\pmod{n_i}$ such that the congruence classes are
disjoint (that is, every integer is $\equiv a_i\pmod{n_i}$ for at most one $1\leq i\leq r$). How
large can $r$ be in terms of $N$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #281
research_problems.statement:
Let $n_1<n_2<\cdots$ be an infinite sequence such that, for any choice of congruence classes
$a_i\pmod{n_i}$, the set of integers not satisfying any of the congruences $a_i\pmod{n_i}$ has
density $0$. Is it true that for every $\epsilon>0$ there exists some $k$ such that, for every
choice of congruence classes $a_i$, the density of integers not satisfying any of the congruences
$a_i\pmod{n_i}$ for $1\leq i\leq k$ is less than $\epsilon$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #279
research_problems.statement:
Let $k\geq 3$. Is there a choice of congruence classes $a_p\pmod{p}$ for every prime $p$
such that all sufficiently large integers can be written as $a_p+tp$ for some prime $p$
and integer $t\geq k$?

title: Primitive sets
summary: A set of integers $>1$ in which no element divides another. Erdős proved $\sum 1/(a\log a)$ is bounded over primitive sets and conjectured the primes maximise it; Lichtman proved this in 2022.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #882
research_problems.statement:
What is the size of the largest $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ such that in the set
$$\left\{ \sum_{a\in S} a : \emptyset\neq S\subseteq A\right\}$$
no two distinct elements divide each other?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #143
research_problems.statement:
Let $A \subseteq (1, \infty)$ be a countably infinite set such that for all $x\neq y\in A$ and
integers $k \geq 1$ we have $|kx - y| \geq 1$.

(a) Does this imply that
$$
\liminf \frac{|A \cap [1,x]|}{x} = 0?
$$

(b) Or
$$
\sum_{x \in A} \frac{1}{x \log x} < \infty,
$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1196
research_problems.statement:
Is it true that, for any $x$, if $A\subset [x,\infty)$ is a primitive set of integers (so that no distinct elements of $A$ divide each other) then$$\sum_{a\in A}\frac{1}{a\log a}< 1+o(1),$$where the $o(1)$ term $\to 0$ as $x\to \infty$?
-

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #164
research_problems.statement:
A set $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ is primitive if no member of $A$ divides another. Is the sum
$$\sum_{n\in A}\frac{1}{n\log n}$$
maximised over all primitive sets when $A$ is the set of primes?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #858
research_problems.statement:
Let $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ be such that there is no solution to $at=b$ with $a,b\in A$ and
the smallest prime factor of $t$ is $>a$. Estimate the maximum of
$$\frac{1}{\log N}\sum_{n\in A}\frac{1}{n}.$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #486
research_problems.statement:
Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$, and for each $n \in A$ choose some
$X_n \subseteq \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$. Let
$B = \{m \in \mathbb{N} : m \not\in X_n \pmod{n} \text{ for all } n \in A \text{ with } m > n\}$.
Must $B$ have a logarithmic density?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #872
research_problems.statement:
(a) Erdős Problem 872, part (i) (weak form): there exists a constant $\epsilon > 0$ such that the
game length is at least $\epsilon \cdot n$ for all sufficiently large $n$.

(b) Erdős Problem 872, part (ii) (strong form): for every $\epsilon > 0$, the game length is at
least $(1-\epsilon) \cdot n / 2$ for all sufficiently large $n$.
